chapter: Billie Holiday, Art Tatum and Chicago hotels
title: Reading books aloud to Art Tatum
summary: He reads books to the near-blind Tatum over beer and it became a regular friendship.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: And as I say, Art Tatum was the intermission piano player. You know he couldn't see very well. He saw just sort of faintly, he saw sort of foggy like. He couldn't hardly discern anything. You know little faint shadows was about all Art could see.
And I mentioned one day to Art that I was reading a book about U boats. Count Von Luckner I think the guy's name was.
Oh my husband had an original drawing of him that he got when he was in Germany as a soldier, yes. He got it in (Aachen as a matter of fact I think, yes.

(Aachen that's where Marian and I were married. I mentioned to Art Tatum about the book how great it was. And oh, I wish I could read it. And I said, well heck man, you know, where do you stay, what hotel? He told me, I've forgotten which one it was. And I said, I'll bring it over. I'll read it to you. Oh, and he was so happy about that.
So I came over and read that book to him and we drank beer and he really appreciated that, you

know. And I was so happy to be able to do that. And that became a regular thing that I would come over and read with Art, I mean for Art. And read these books dear friends to him you know. And we were really you know. Musically and human beings up until he died. Because he always used to talk about that. I know when he met Marian he used to talk about it. "Did Jimmy ever used to tell you he used to read for me all the time?"
I'm sure he was very appreciative.
Well Jimmy, I enjoyed it too. Because I liked to read anyway. But to be able to do something for Art you know, what can you do. Art was something.
